title: Gather: an Interdependence Day Potluck
description:
Gather: an Interdependence Potluck on Wednesday, July 2nd | 6:00–8:30pm at Wilshire Park (4116 NE 33rd Ave, Portland 97212)

Brown Hope and Lulove Healing are hosting a Gather: an Interdependence Day Potluck, an invitation to build community in the spirit of interdependence and collective resilience.

Gather with us to share an intimate moment of giving and receiving care, respect, and love. Join us in nourishing our bodies and souls with a shared meal, and you’re encouraged to bring your favorite dish! There will be vegan and gluten free options. 

We’ll have interactive icebreaker activities to help people meet and socialize. Experienced song circle facilitators will lead us in songs and drumming that honor our values of freedom, justice, healing, and liberation.

Gather is also an opportunity to shine a light on the truth about this nation’s long history of injustice. July 4th is a day that carries a lot of traumatic the United States. The holiday often glazes over the slavery, colonialism, and genocide that this nation was built upon, and the present day inequities that persist due to the lack of accountability and resolution. 

Brown Hope Founder and CEO, cameron whitten, will perform a live reenactment of the 1852 speech “What to the Slave is Your 4th of July?” by civil rights leader Frederick Douglass.

We’ll have a facilitated group dialogue after the speech and brainstorm ideas about how to increase our collective power and foster a more interdependent Portland community that’s actively working towards racial justice. 

Gather is free and open to the public. We welcome people of all racial backgrounds, as well as uplifting Black, Brown, and Indigenous leadership on our journey towards collective liberation.

#GatherPDX #BeTheFire

description:
Good Trouble Lives On is a national day of nonviolent action to respond to the attacks posed on our civil and human rights by the Trump administration and to remind them that in America, the power lies with the people. 

On July 17, the anniversary of Congressman John Lewis’s passing, we’re taking action across the country to defend our democracy and carry forward his legacy of Good Trouble.

From voter suppression bills like the SAVE Act to the criminalization of protest, the Trump administration is launching a full-scale attack on our civil and human rights. But we know the truth: in America, the power lies with the people, and we’re rising to prove it.

This is more than a protest; it’s a moral reckoning. A continuation of the movement Lewis helped lead, and a new front in the struggle for freedom.

title: Standing on the corner for PEACE and democracy in Estacada
description:
Every Saturday from 11:00 AM to 12:00 PM, we gather for an hour of peaceful visibility on the corner of Highway 224 and City Hall in Downtown Estacada.

We’d like to believe we’re standing in peace — but these days, we’re standing in protest and for our democracy.

It’s fun. It’s energizing. And honestly? It’s better than doing nothing.
This may be our last chance to stand up for our rights — locally, visibly, and together. No one’s coming to save us. It’s up to us to lead. And the best place to start is right here in our own community.

✨ What to expect:
– Supportive honks and waves from passing cars
– Friendly conversation and good company
– Bring a sign if you want — or just bring yourself
– It’s only one hour, but it means something

It might feel small — but it’s something. And sometimes something is everything. Please join us. There’s real power in showing up

title: Disappeared in America - Redmond, WA
description:

**In America, the government doesn’t get to grab people off the streets, skip the courtroom, and send them straight to a foreign prison.** Disappeared in America is a national day of action to stand up for the rule of law and confront the Trump administration’s illegal abductions, detentions, and deportations of people like Kilmar Abrego Garcia, Rui Marras, and Juan Maldonado Zuniga. 

🚨**On Thursday, June 26th, we’re showing up at courthouses and town squares across the country to say: in America, we don’t let the government disappear people. That’s not who we are.**🚨

Americans believe in rule of law —and the courts are saying that due process is required. If a president can ignore the courts and disappear lawful residents, there is no limit to what can come next. President Trump has said he wants to abduct and deport U.S. citizens. If this isn’t stopped now, no one is safe.

**On June 26th we are launching a national photo petition day where people will take photos with posters of those who have been disappeared and flood social media with the truth.** 

A key focal point of this campaign will be to call on local sheriffs to refuse to cooperate with directives from ICE to engage in federal immigration enforcement, such as renting jail beds to ICE, participating in immigration raids, and transferring people to ICE detentions.  Sheriffs have wide discretion in how much they cooperate with ICE. Participation in federal immigration activities places additional burden on sheriffs’ offices and can erode local community trust in local law enforcement.

description:
Join Camel City United Indivisible for our monthly community meeting as we welcome special guest Brajan Funes, a local organizer and advocate who will speak about Temporary Protected Status (TPS) and the urgent fight for migrant justice.

📣 TPS is under threat.
For over 25 years, tens of thousands of Honduran nationals have lived and worked in the U.S. under TPS — including many of our neighbors in North Carolina. Their futures hang in the balance as their protections expire this July.

“We’ve had 25 years of them giving us TPS. And for them to say that they’re going to cancel it, it’s a big hit,” says G., a longtime NC resident currently in sensitive immigration proceedings.
“You have a hope for all those years that they might give you residency.”

Together, we’ll discuss:

What TPS means for our communities

The risks facing families if TPS is revoked

How we can support advocacy efforts for permanent protections

🗣️ This meeting is open to all. Learn, connect, and take action as we continue building a just and inclusive Forsyth County.

title: Reclaim Idaho 2025 Summer Update Zoom - Tues (6/17)
description:
Please join us for a statewide update zoom to get an update on the fight against voucher expansion. On June 17th, we’ll be meeting at 6:30pm MT / 5:30pm PT to discuss the crisis of private school vouchers in Idaho and what we're doing about it.
 
During the 2025 legislative session, Idaho lawmakers passed House Bill 93 and enacted a $50 million school-voucher program. For the first time in state history, Idaho tax dollars will be used to subsidize the cost of tuition for private-school families. 

The special-interest groups promoting vouchers have made clear that the $50 million program is only the beginning. During next year’s legislative session, they intend to remove the $50-million cap and expand the program to all private-school families, including the wealthy, at an estimated cost of $339 million per year.
 
Such a massive expansion of vouchers would bankrupt Idaho and drain millions from public schools. For the benefit of a small number of private-school families, it would defund the public education system that serves 94% of Idaho’s kids. 

It may be inevitable that the legislature tries to expand House Bill 93, but it is not inevitable that they will succeed. To stop this attack on public schools, we need to get organized. Please sign up if you can make it and we hope to see you soon!

Daniel was a survivor of the 2011 Tucson shooting and was the first to administer first aid before EMTs arrived on the scene. Turning tragedy into resilience, Daniel decided to live a life of public service to protect Arizonan families and served on the Sunnyside School board (2011-2015) and was later elected to the Arizona State Legislature (2017-2022). Now, Daniel is running for Congress to Fight the Trump Administration to protect Arizonans' social security and healthcare access, expand federal dollars into public education, and lower the cost of everyday goods and housing.

title: GOOD TROUBLE LIVES ON: Birmingham Al
description:
Good Trouble Lives On is a national day of nonviolent action to respond to the attacks posed on our civil and human rights by the Trump administration and to remind them that in America, the power lies with the people. 

On July 17, the anniversary of Congressman John Lewis’s passing, we’re taking action across the country to defend our democracy and carry forward his legacy of Good Trouble.

From voter suppression bills like the SAVE Act to the criminalization of protest, the Trump administration is launching a full-scale attack on our civil and human rights. But we know the truth: in America, the power lies with the people, and we’re rising to prove it.

This is more than a protest; it’s a moral reckoning. A continuation of the movement Lewis helped lead, and a new front in the struggle for freedom.

**Please note:** A core principle behind our Good Trouble Lives On actions is a commitment to nonviolence in all we do. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.

title: Weekly (Tues) I-91 Overpass Standout - Mtn Park Rd, Holyoke, MA
description:
Come out to show that ordinary people can raise their voices against the chaos and destruction of this Administration. Help remind folks that they, too, can stand up for their beliefs - and that there's lots and lots of people who aren't on board with the "cruelty as entertainment" behavior of Trump and Musk and the GOP.

### Recent DOT Visits

A Department of Transportation employee has visited twice in the past three weeks prior to 5/20 to ask that people NOT attach anything to the fencing. On 5/20, he parked and waited until everything was removed from the fencing. It seems reasonable to expect that DOT enforcement will continue.

### How to Get There

The address "9 Mountain Park Rd, Holyoke" will get you there if you're using Waze. (Mountain Park Road runs off Route 5, and is not accessible from I-91.) People have reported that some GPS systems bring you right under the bridge, but on I-91. That’s annoying!

Please park on the side of the road before the bridge. We can't park on the bridge.

### Other Stuff

Please take everything you brought away with you, and leave the site totally clean.

If rain is predicted, we'll cancel. If we cancel, you'll receive an email notification.

We may see a counter protester. If so, the best thing to do is just ignore them and spend our time and energy waving to motorists. Let's keep things 100% non-confrontational in words and body language.

### A Few Requests

We've found that roof rake sections make wonderful flagpoles and banner poles. If you have a roof rake (or 10’-15’ light metal poles or conduit) to contribute, we'll be happy to take it off your hands!

Donations...we've purchased banners and grommets and flags and zip ties and bungee cords, and we'll be getting more. We’ve purchased 20” x 30” letter boards for messaging we can change. All this costs $$$. We'll have a bucket for donations, and if you could throw something in, that'd be great. And if not, that's perfectly OK, too - your presence is what's really important. See where the money's going! https://tinyurl.com/IN-SLWMProtestTeamFinancials
